capabilities.status_reason: ios-accessibility adds synchronous setters for accessibility element status, label, hint, and value, a synchronous `isAccessibilityElement` property read, nullable label/hint/value presence checks, and seventeen UIKit traits on a borrowed, caller-owned UIView. The adapter requires the UIKit main thread and is !Send/!Sync; trait updates replace the full mask and may override UIKit defaults. Adjustable requires accessibilityIncrement and accessibilityDecrement; NotEnabled requires a view that does not respond to input; KeyboardKey requires key behavior; UpdatesFrequently and PlaysSound rely on host-owned value updates and activation sound; CausesPageTurn requires host page-turn behavior via accessibilityScroll:; StartsMediaSession applies only when activation starts a media session; AllowsDirectInteraction applies only to caller-marked content that supports direct touch; SummaryElement requires caller-supplied summary content. The adapter routes no input, configures no DirectTouchOptions, adds no callback or audio behavior, makes no presentation-timing promise, reports only the accessibility-element property (not visibility or focus); its nullable text-property checks return no text, empty strings count as present, and UIKit defaults do not prove caller assignment; it makes no live VoiceOver claim. B120 checks membership for a requested known trait without exposing the raw mask or unknown flags. B123 gets and sets the child-elements-hidden property through an iOS 5.0+ selector guard; absent selectors return `AccessibilityApiUnavailable` without raising the package's iOS 4.0 floor. It does not set the receiver's own element flag, visual hidden state, or interaction state. B126 reads/writes `shouldGroupAccessibilityChildren` under an iOS 6.0 selector guard for logical parent groups; B129 reads/writes `accessibilityViewIsModal` under an iOS 5.0 selector guard for actually modal accessible content. Neither claims assistive traversal, view presentation, or app modality. B132 adds selector-guarded `set_accessibility_language(Option<&str>)` and `has_accessibility_language()` for UIKit BCP 47 `accessibilityLanguage`; `None` clears, other input passes unchanged without validation/normalization, and the getter does not report effective assistive-app language or invoke the iOS 17 callback. B135 adds selector-guarded `accessibility_responds_to_user_interaction()` and `set_accessibility_responds_to_user_interaction(bool)` for the iOS 13.0 `accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction` property; its default can derive from other accessibility properties, and the setter creates no interaction handler. B138 adds selector-guarded `AccessibilityNavigationStyle` getter/setter with `Automatic`, `Separate`, and `Combined`; unknown native values are returned as `None`, not raw integers. The iOS 8.0 property currently affects Switch Control only, not VoiceOver, and does not raise the package iOS 4.0 floor. B141 adds selector-guarded `set_accessibility_textual_context(Option<AccessibilityTextualContext>)` and `has_accessibility_textual_context()` for iOS 13.0 `accessibilityTextualContext`. The enum maps seven named UIKit `NSString` constants; `None` clears, and the methods neither invoke the iOS 17 callback nor claim assistive output. B144 adds selector-guarded `accessibility_container_type()` and `set_accessibility_container_type(AccessibilityContainerType)` at iOS 11.0 for `Unspecified`, `List`, and `Landmark`; unknown values map to `None`. `DataTable` needs `UIAccessibilityContainerDataTable`, and iOS 13 `SemanticGroup` is excluded without per-value availability handling. B147 declines `accessibilityDirectTouchOptions` because its VoiceOver passthrough/audio behavior needs a dedicated direct-touch contract. B150 adds iOS 13 `accessibilityUserInputLabels` set and non-empty-presence operations behind selector guards; it sends an explicit array even for empty input, may observe UIKit defaults, and claims no speech recognition match or iOS 17 callback behavior. B153 adds selector-guarded iOS 5 `accessibilityActivationPoint` getter/setter over `CGPoint` screen coordinates; UIKit defaults to the midpoint of `accessibilityFrame`, callers must recompute after layout or screen-position changes, and no assistive activation outcome is promised. B156 adds selector-guarded iOS 11 `accessibilityAttributedLabel` set and non-empty-presence operations over `NSAttributedString`; UIKit copies the value and couples it to `accessibilityLabel`, and the adapter invokes no iOS 17 callback or claims speech behavior. B159 adds selector-guarded iOS 11 `accessibilityAttributedHint` set and non-empty-presence operations over `NSAttributedString`; UIKit copies the value and couples it to `accessibilityHint`, and the adapter invokes no iOS 17 callback or claims speech behavior. B162 adds selector-guarded iOS 11 `accessibilityAttributedValue` set and non-empty-presence operations over `NSAttributedString`; UIKit copies the value and couples it to `accessibilityValue`, and the adapter invokes no iOS 17 callback or claims speech behavior. B171 adds selector-guarded iOS 7 `accessibilityPath` set and non-empty-presence operations using `UIBezierPath` screen coordinates; callers own geometry updates, and no assistive highlighting or activation result is claimed. B174 adds selector-guarded `accessibilityFrame` getter/setter over screen-coordinate `CGRect`. UIKit does not declare an explicit minimum for this property; selector checks preserve the package floor, and no conversion, layout, visibility, assistive-output result, or `UIAccessibilityElement` container-space behavior for `UIView` is claimed. B177 adds selector-guarded iOS 5 `UIAccessibilityIdentification.accessibilityIdentifier` get/set; the getter returns owned text or `None`, and the setter clears with `None`. It is UI Automation metadata, not a label, uniqueness guarantee, or assistive-output contract. `accessibilityFrameInContainerSpace` is excluded because the binding exposes it on `UIAccessibilityElement`, not `UIView`. B180 adds `UIAccessibilityTraitTabBar` (iOS 10.0) for a view that represents an ordered tab list; the caller separately sets `isAccessibilityElement` to false. The methods do not call `accessibilityExpandedStatusBlock` or expand/collapse content, and the block can take precedence. capabilities.status_reason: ios-files implements sandbox file reads, writes, directory operations, removal, and existence checks with descriptor-relative no-follow traversal, plus synchronous adoption of URLSession temporary downloads by staged copy and atomic rename to AppPath. A concurrent native directory rename can move an opened directory outside the selected root, so containment is not guaranteed under that race. B128 adds `IosFiles::directory_entry_count`, which counts direct names except `.` and `..` across all entry kinds and byte names without building a Rust-owned listing or doing per-entry kind lookups. It is O(n), libc may allocate, and concurrent changes can affect the result; it is not an atomic snapshot, reservation, or deletion guard. B131 adds `IosFiles::directory_is_empty`, which stops at the first direct name other than `.` and `..` when nonempty. Both directory queries are best-effort under concurrent mutation; emptiness is not a delete guard. B134 adds `IosFiles::directory_entry_kind_counts` for regular-file, directory, and `Other` totals using no-follow per-name classification. It includes non-UTF-8 names and returns an error rather than partial counts if an enumerated name vanishes; it is not an atomic snapshot or delete guard. B137 adds `IosFiles::volume_available_capacity_bytes(AppDirectory)` from checked `f_bavail * f_bsize` on the retained root descriptor. This is a volume-wide point-in-time value, not an app quota, reservation, or write guarantee. Apple classifies `fstatfs` under required-reason `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace`; the host must declare an approved reason matching actual use in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, and the library adds no manifest. B140 declines `NSURLDirectoryEntryCountKey` as a cheap-count API: it is optional and filesystem-dependent, while descriptor `ATTR_DIR_ENTRYCOUNT` is 32-bit, may be expensive, and is not supported by every volume format. B128/B131 remain the deterministic direct-count and early-stop paths. B143 declines `f_bfree` as a separate app-facing value because it includes reserved filesystem blocks that the sandbox cannot consume; B137 already reports `f_bavail` for non-superusers. B146 adds `IosFiles::volume_total_capacity_bytes(AppDirectory)` from checked `f_blocks * f_bsize` on the retained root descriptor. It describes the mounted volume, not physical-device capacity or an app quota, and shares B137's required-reason Disk Space privacy-manifest obligation. B149 declines `f_files`/`f_ffree` as app-specific capacity: these are volume-wide node counts, not an app/container budget, and `f_ffree` does not establish whether a later sandbox create will succeed. Actual creation remains authoritative. User-selected/provider URLs are unsupported. B235 adds `IosFiles::directory_allocated_size_snapshot(AppPath)` from descriptor-bound `fgetattrlist(ATTR_DIR_ALLOCSIZE)`, reporting bytes used by the directory object only, not descendants, quota, reservation, or performance. Host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. B237 declines `ATTR_DIR_DATALENGTH` because it measures the directory object, not child contents, and adds no supported operation. B238 declines `ATTR_DIR_IOBLOCKSIZE` because the facade has no directory-data I/O or buffer control. B240 declines `ATTR_DIR_LINKCOUNT` because it is not a child-directory count and B134 already counts direct subdirectories. B241 declines `ATTR_DIR_MOUNTSTATUS` because no mount or recursive traversal operation consumes it. B242 adds `IosFiles::regular_file_total_fork_size_snapshot(AppPath)` from descriptor-bound `fgetattrlist(ATTR_FILE_TOTALSIZE)`. It reports logical bytes across all forks for one regular file; it does not expose fork contents, only the data-fork read size, or physical allocation. Host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. B244 adds `IosFiles::regular_file_data_fork_allocated_size_snapshot(AppPath)` from descriptor-bound `fgetattrlist(ATTR_FILE_DATAALLOCSIZE)`, reporting bytes allocated for the data fork only and excluding resource-fork allocation. It does not convert B109 `st_blocks`, claim exact physical device use, or expose fork contents. Host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. B247 declines `ATTR_FILE_FORKCOUNT`: it reports only a fork count, not fork names, sizes, or access, and no facade operation consumes it. B248 adds `IosFiles::regular_file_resource_fork_allocated_size_snapshot(AppPath)` from descriptor-bound `fgetattrlist(ATTR_FILE_RSRCALLOCSIZE)`, reporting bytes allocated for the resource fork only. It reads no fork contents, and zero does not establish fork absence. Host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. B247 declines `ATTR_FILE_FORKCOUNT` because no fork-enumeration or fork-operation contract consumes the value. B251 adds `IosFiles::regular_file_resource_fork_size_snapshot(AppPath)` from descriptor-bound `fgetattrlist(ATTR_FILE_RSRCLENGTH)`, reporting logical bytes in the resource fork only. Zero does not prove absence; it exposes no fork enumeration, access, or contents. Host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`. B253 declines `ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE`: it adds another all-fork allocation scalar while B109 already exposes per-entry `st_blocks` and B244/B248 expose data/resource-fork allocation; no app-data operation needs the duplicate value, and no fixed conversion is assumed. B256 declines `ATTR_FILE_IOBLOCKSIZE` because no exposed stream, buffer, or policy consumes the optimal directory/file I/O hint; it is not an alignment or performance guarantee. B257 declines `ATTR_FILE_FORKLIST` because Apple documents an undefined attrreference payload, so no stable typed fork-list parser is possible. B259 declines obsolete HFS-specific `ATTR_FILE_DATAEXTENTS`/`ATTR_FILE_RSRCEXTENTS` because they expose at most eight possibly inaccurate extents and Apple directs new clients not to use them. B260 declines obsolete `ATTR_FILE_CLUMPSIZE` because no allocation or streaming-write policy consumes this nonbinding hint. B262 declines `ATTR_FILE_FILETYPE` because the SDK says it is always zero and reserved; B263 declines `ATTR_FILE_DEVTYPE` because special-file operations are absent and B122 already represents `st_rdev`; B264 declines `ATTR_FILE_LINKCOUNT` because B105 already reports regular-file link count; B265 declines `ATTR_FILE_DATALENGTH` because B90 already reports the no-follow data-fork logical length, while B242/B251 cover all-fork and resource-fork lengths. The value tracks a document across moves and is sticky to its assigned path across safe saves, but is not an inode, content hash, clone ID, link ID, cross-volume identity, or durability guarantee. Host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy; see PLAN_IOS_FILE_DOCUMENT_ID.md B272 adds `IosFiles::entry_added_time(AppPath)` from descriptor-bound `fgetattrlist(ATTR_CMN_ADDEDTIME)` for regular files. XNU defines the value as file creation or rename into a containing directory and warns of inconsistent values for hard-linked items; it is not a reliable creation-time or path-history record. Host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`; see PLAN_IOS_FILE_ADDED_TIME.md. B275 adds `IosFiles::regular_file_data_generation_snapshot(AppPath)` with the device/inode identity from `fstat` and `ATTR_CMN_GEN_COUNT` from `fgetattrlist` on the same opened regular-file descriptor. XNU says compare only nonzero counts for the same filesystem object; zero is invalid and occurs for memory-mapped files, so the API returns `None`. This is not a general change token or persistent identity; host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`; see PLAN_IOS_FILE_DATA_GENERATION.md. B296 adds `IosFiles::entry_object_kind(AppPath)`, one detailed `st_mode & S_IFMT` snapshot via `fstatat(..., AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`. It distinguishes regular files, directories, symlinks, FIFOs, sockets, block devices, and character devices while preserving other type bits as `Unknown(u32)`; it does not open/follow the final entry or alter portable `FileKind`. The result is point-in-time, retains the concurrent-parent-rename limit, and uses File Timestamp required-reason APIs, so the host must declare an applicable approved reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`; see `PLAN_IOS_ENTRY_OBJECT_KIND.md`. B301 adds `IosFiles::entry_stored_backup_time(AppPath)` for regular files and directories using descriptor-bound `fgetattrlist(ATTR_CMN_BKUPTIME)`. It preserves the filesystem-stored signed seconds and nanoseconds only; this marker is not proof of OS, iCloud, or other backup completion, inclusion, freshness, durability, or recoverability, and the API does not set it or perform backup work. Unsupported attributes remain `Unsupported`; host use requires an applicable approved File Timestamp reason in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`; see `PLAN_IOS_FILE_BACKUP_TIME_MARKER.md`. B529 adds source-compatible `FileBackend::append` and `Files::append` with an explicit `Unsupported` default that does not mutate older backends. The iOS implementation opens descriptor-relative files with `O_APPEND | O_NOFOLLOW` and issues one write; an error may leave an unknown prefix, concurrent successful slices remain contiguous with unspecified order, and success does not imply crash durability. B529 does not resolve B524 backup-exclusion metadata. B563 adds source-compatible `Files::create_directories` with an `Unsupported` default and an iOS `mkdirat`/`openat` implementation anchored to retained app-directory descriptors. Existing directories succeed; non-directory and symlink components fail; an error can leave earlier created components in place. Host regressions cover nested/idempotent creation, file collisions, symlink escape, and legacy backends.
